children: The company reports record quarterly EBITDA of Rs 2,509 million as Ex-US markets grow 31 per cent year-on-year, exceeding US revenue for the first time

Strides Pharma Science Limited reported a 17.1 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 14,297 million in Q2 FY27, driven by strong growth in its Ex-US markets, which surpassed its US business in quarterly revenue for the first time. For the quarter ended 30 September 2026, the Bengaluru-based pharmaceutical company also recorded its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA of Rs 2,509 million, marking an 8.4 per cent increase over the corresponding period last year.

The company's EBITDA margin stood at 17.6 per cent, compared with 19 per cent in Q2 FY26, reflecting higher input material, freight and operating costs. Operational profit after tax (PAT) increased 11.5 per cent to Rs 1,358 million, while reported PAT grew 2 per cent to Rs 1,341 million.

Revenue from Ex-US markets increased 31 per cent year-on-year to Rs 6,963 million, compared with Rs 6,855 million from the US business, which grew 9 per cent. This marked the first time Ex-US quarterly revenue exceeded US revenue. The company also launched three products in the US during the quarter.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue rose 15.1 per cent to Rs 26,951 million, while EBITDA increased 6.9 per cent to Rs 4,807 million. Operational PAT grew 9.8 per cent to Rs 2,589 million, while reported PAT increased 26.4 per cent to Rs 2,996 million. However, gross margin declined to 56 per cent in Q2 FY27 from 57.8 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year, reflecting a contraction of 180 basis points.

Badree Komandur, Managing Director and Group CEO of Strides Pharma Science, said the company's diversification strategy continued to support growth, with Ex-US markets emerging as a significant revenue contributor. He said the company was addressing higher raw material, freight and operating expenses through cost optimisation initiatives.

Komandur also highlighted an increase of Rs 2,114 million in net debt during H1 FY27, attributed to an elongated cash-to-cash cycle and higher inventory holdings to navigate market conditions. The company expects its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to stabilise by the end of the financial year. Strides also announced the appointment of Biren Gabhawala as an Independent Director, citing his experience in financial reporting, audit and corporate governance.
